author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell's guest pointed out that Britain has churned through seven prime ministers in just over a decade, arguing that kind of instability scares away the investment the country desperately needs. He posed a simple question, asking whether anyone starting from scratch today would deliberately design two nearly identical parties controlled by the same financial interests. He warned that even a fresh face like Andy Burnham would eventually disappoint, not because of the man himself, but because the entire system is built to fail the people it claims to serve. Is this really the democracy Britain would choose if it were starting over today?

description:

author: Russell Brand
description:
Mikki Willis says his brother David was stable and healthy for years while living with AIDS, until a new drug called AZT was introduced and everything changed. David grew thin, lost muscle mass and was vomiting daily, and members of his community began calling his mother begging her to take him off the medicine. When she raised concerns with doctors, she was told it was simply his body adjusting, and that Anthony Fauci was too far ahead of the science to question. David died of pneumonia not long after. Was his death simply bad luck, or could it have been prevented?

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell's guest drew a straight line from cable television's business model to the legal system itself, arguing both were built to manufacture problems people would keep paying to solve. God gave humanity one law in the garden and it was broken almost immediately, then ten, then hundreds, then billions of pages of legislation that seemed designed to be broken and to benefit whoever was writing them. Yet Jesus reduced it all back down to two simple commands, to love God and love your neighbor. Was the entire legal system ever really about justice, or just another version of the same old racket?
